title: Influence of peripheral inflammation on the blood-brain barrier assessed via quantitative MRI
summary: The study investigates whether peripheral low‑grade inflammation alters blood‑brain barrier (BBB) permeability and thus facilitates neuropsychiatric symptoms. In healthy volunteers—vaccinated against Covid‑19 outside the scope of this study on the independent recommendation of their treating physicians—the immunization induces a mild immune activation that transiently releases pro‑inflammatory cytokines. Quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (qMRI) is employed to approximate BBB permeability. The results could reveal new therapeutic targets for affective disorders with an inflammatory component and inform future personalized prevention and treatment strategies for psychiatric diseases.
conditions: We will only examine healthy controls.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	healthy participants, who have a planned Covid-19 vaccination or healthy participants without a planned Covid-19 vaccination
•	Age between 18 and 65 years
Exclusion criteria:
•	Current mental disorders requiring treatment
•	Severe somatic diseases (such as pneumonia, sepsis, stroke, liver/kidney transplant, thyroid disorders are included only if TSH is normal)
•	Current pregnancy or breastfeeding 
•	MRI exclusion criteria: tattoos in the neck/head area, permanent make-up, magnetically attached dentures, metallic/magnetic implants (pacemaker, defibrillator, joint endoprosthesis, heart valve, stent, metal, silicone, vascular/surgical clips, vascular endoprosthesis, metal pins, skin chips, garnet/other metal splinters, insulin pump, painkiller pump, neurostimulator, hearing implant)
•	Exclusion criteria for contrast agent (CA) administration: elevated creatinin level, liver transplant, kidney transplant, gadovist allergies
•	Fever, severe infection symptoms, urinary tract infection within the last 7 days before T1
•	Antibiotic treatment within the last 14 days before T1
